findings.failure_scenario: A project that already contains a CSV document (saved JSON has original_file.mime_type = "text/csv") is opened after this change: Project.documents() -> Document.all_children_of_parent_path -> load_from_file -> Document.model_validate runs FileInfo.validate_mime_type (extraction.py:299-307), which now raises ValueError("MIME type is not supported: text/csv ..."). The ValidationError propagates out of get_documents (document_api.py:250-255), so GET /api/projects/{id}/documents fails (422 via the custom ValidationError handler) and the library UI shows zero documents; get_document/delete_document/extract/run_extractor_config all load via from_id_and_parent_path (basemodel.py:543-564) and fail the same way, so the stored CSV document cannot even be viewed or deleted through the app anymore.
findings.summary: Removing "text/csv" from SUPPORTED_MIME_TYPES invalidates documents already persisted with that mime type, so loading them raises and breaks the whole project document listing, not just CSV uploads.

findings.failure_scenario: get_kind_from_mime_type("text/csv") (extraction.py:407-411) now returns None and FileInfo rejects the mime type, but GeminiExtractor._get_kind_from_mime_type("text/csv") (gemini_extractor.py:98-102) still returns Kind.DOCUMENT and _extract (line 104) happily sends the CSV to Gemini. A consumer of the published kiln-ai library calling GeminiExtractor.extract(path, "text/csv") — exactly the case the deleted paid test test_extract_csv covered — still gets a successful extraction, and the csv entry removed from test_get_kind_from_mime_type's parametrize list means no test pins either behavior; the repository now has two contradictory MIME-type registries.
findings.summary: The CSV removal is incomplete: the Gemini extractor still lists "text/csv" in MIME_TYPES_SUPPORTED, so it continues to classify and extract CSV documents while the datamodel/API/UI now declare CSV unsupported; the test edits hide this divergence instead of removing the support.

findings.failure_scenario: create_document (document_api.py:208-222) calls guess_mime_type(file.filename) and raises 422 before touching the uploaded bytes, so test_content is never used. The test still fails to even start if the CSV asset is renamed/removed or the fixture changes; the neighboring test_create_document_content_type_detection shows the simpler form (pass b"test content", drop the mock_file_factory dependency and the anyio import) that exercises the identical 422 path.
findings.summary: The new rejection test unnecessarily reads the CSV fixture through anyio and depends on tests/assets/document_people.csv, even though the endpoint derives the mime type only from the filename and never inspects the request body before rejecting it.
